parts.text: Which claim correctly classifies the elements among these samples?

options.text: Copper and oxygen gas are elements because each is a pure substance made of only one kind of identical particle.
Distilled water is an element because it is a pure liquid used in the lab.
Only solids can be elements, so oxygen gas cannot be an element.
Copper is an element only when it is mixed with other metals.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Hamza sorts three pure samples in the lab: copper metal made of only copper particles, distilled water made of hydrogen and oxygen joined together, and a sealed jar of oxygen gas made of only oxygen particles.

part_answers.answer: An element is a pure substance of one kind of particle; copper and oxygen fit that, while water joins two elements and is a compound, and being solid or mixed is not the test.

teacher.key_rationale: An element is a pure substance of only one kind of identical particle. Copper and oxygen qualify; water is a compound. Purity as a liquid, solid-only rules, or requiring a mixture all miss the element hinge.
